Ticker tape.short_definition: Continuously supply recurring numeric prices to smart contracts; a specialized inbound oracle price feed.

Oracle.short_definition: Off-chain components observe contract requests/state and submit external data to the blockchain in a transaction.

Reverse Oracle.short_definition: Off-chain components observe specific on-chain state/events and react outside the blockchain; outbound information flow.

Pull-based inbound oracle.short_definition: Bring external data on-chain by an active component fetching it manually or on demand (pull).

Push-based inbound oracle.short_definition: An external component automatically pushes data on-chain without an explicit contract request.

State Channel.short_definition: Multiple users exchange microtransactions off-chain and periodically anchor their hash on-chain for later proof.

Off-chain Contract Registry.short_definition: A contract registers references to off-chain services/versions for discovery and versioning.

Legal and smart contract pair.short_definition: Link an off-chain legal contract to an on-chain smart contract, retaining signatures/states on-chain and sensitive data off-chain.

Off-chain data storage.short_definition: Store bulky data off-chain and its hash on-chain to verify integrity with less storage and disclosure.

Confidential and pseudo-anonymous contra.short_definition: Combine an off-chain legal contract, on-chain state machine and zero-knowledge proofs to verify clauses without exposing private data.

Off-chain Signatures.short_definition: Sign authorization/data off-chain and verify/recover the cryptographic signature on-chain to avoid extra transactions.

Delegated Computation.short_definition: Delegate expensive computation off-chain, submit results on-chain and allow a challenge/verification period.

Master & Sub Key.short_definition: Derive multiple purpose-specific subkeys from a master key hierarchically (BIP32) instead of reusing a sensitive key.

Hot & Cold Wallet Storage.short_definition: Separate frequently used online funds from secure offline reserves, optionally with multisignatures and withdrawal delays.

Key Sharding.short_definition: Split a private key into shares, requiring a threshold of shares to reconstruct it.

X-confirmation.short_definition: Wait for X block confirmations before accepting a transaction as final to mitigate chain reorganizations.

Blockchain BP Engine.short_definition: An on-chain smart contract stores and executes a collaborative business workflow.

Smart Contract Activities.short_definition: One smart contract contains multiple business-process activities and controls transitions between them.

Decentralize business process.short_definition: Use blockchain to coordinate a collaborative process across organizations without a trusted intermediary.

Identifier Registry.short_definition: Map a decentralized identifier (DID) to off-chain attributes in a contract; private-key possession proves control.

Multiple Registration.short_definition: One controller creates multiple distinct identifiers to prevent correlation between identity contexts.

Bound with Social Media.short_definition: Bind an on-chain identifier to a social-media account with proof of possession.

Dual Resolution.short_definition: Resolve identities bidirectionally so two DID-identified entities can communicate.

Delegate List.short_definition: Register delegated addresses that can help recover a DID when its controlling private key is lost.

Blockchain Security Pattern for Big Data.short_definition: Record operations on a big-data repository using blockchain for audit and traceability.

Blockchain-based reputation system.short_definition: Record and update participant reputation/trust scores on-chain with verifiable behavioral history.

Vote.short_definition: Collaborative verifiable on-chain governance decisions through proposals and votes.

Blocklist.short_definition: A contract lists addresses prohibited from calling specified functions.

Announcement.short_definition: Publish and retrieve verifiable public announcements on-chain.

Bulletin Board.short_definition: An on-chain public message board lets users publish/query immutable, verifiable messages.

Randomness.short_definition: Generate secure verifiable randomness in a deterministic blockchain, e.g. VRF.

Poll.short_definition: Collect and tally participants' opinions/preferences through on-chain polls.

Selective Content Generation.short_definition: Conditionally generate/reveal content according to authorization or on-chain state.

Time-Constrained Access.short_definition: A contract authorizes access to a resource only within a specified time window.

One-Off Access.short_definition: Grant one-use access and mark the permission/token consumed to prevent reuse.

Digital Record.short_definition: Record document metadata/hashes on-chain as proof of existence and integrity over time.

State machine.short_definition: Represent contract phases and allowed transitions explicitly as a state machine.

Proxy contract.short_definition: Forward calls to a replaceable implementation contract to upgrade logic while retaining the public address.

Contract Registry (on-chain).short_definition: Map multiple contracts to their latest version addresses; unlike a proxy forwarding to one target.

Factory contract.short_definition: A creator contract creates new instances of other smart contracts; deployment primitives alone are insufficient.

Data contract.short_definition: Keep persistent data in a dedicated contract separate from business logic, allowing logic upgrades without migrating state.

Router contract.short_definition: Route function calls to different contracts/modules based on a function selector.

Relay contract.short_definition: Forward users' off-chain signed meta-transactions and pay gas for them.

Emergency stop.short_definition: Temporarily pause sensitive contract functions during anomalous behavior or attacks (circuit breaker).

Mortal.short_definition: Terminate a contract using selfdestruct; historical code/storage removal is restricted by EIP-6780.

Check-Effects-Interactions.short_definition: Check preconditions, update internal state, then interact externally to prevent reentrancy.

Mutex.short_definition: Explicitly lock/unlock sensitive contract execution to prevent concurrent or recursive calls to shared resources.

Guard check.short_definition: Validate preconditions with modifiers/require before executing a function to prevent invalid or unauthorized calls.

Rate limit.short_definition: Limit operation frequency/volume within a time interval (speed bump) to mitigate abuse or mass withdrawals.

Balance limit.short_definition: Cap funds held by a contract to limit financial exposure if compromised.

Low contract footprint.short_definition: Reduce on-chain contract computation and storage footprint to lower gas; network packet optimization alone is different.

Loop unrolling.short_definition: Replace dynamic loops with fixed instruction sequences to reduce unpredictable gas consumption.

Contract size limit.short_definition: Split oversized contract bytecode into modules to satisfy deployment size constraints such as EIP-170.

Off-chain computation.short_definition: Move expensive blockchain computation off-chain, submitting and verifying the result on-chain.

State anchoring.short_definition: Periodically anchor a digest/Merkle root of off-chain states/transactions on-chain for integrity verification.

Data refresh.short_definition: Refresh stale on-chain data using external transactions, potentially rewarding callers (incentive execution).

Ownable.short_definition: A single owner address can execute restricted administrative contract functions.

Role-based control.short_definition: Assign roles to addresses and enforce different permissions for each role (RBAC).

Permissioned actions.short_definition: Restrict sensitive contract functions to a predefined set of authorized addresses.

Implicit authorization.short_definition: Authorize implicitly through asset/token ownership (balanceOf/ownerOf), without an explicit permission list.

Limited-access.short_definition: Restrict contract functions with an access modifier that rejects unauthorized addresses.

Immutable data.short_definition: Use constant/immutable values fixed after deployment to avoid storage reads and save gas.

Mutable data.short_definition: Contract state values can change over time through updates/setters, unlike immutable data.

Append-only data.short_definition: Only append new records; never overwrite/remove prior records, preserving a complete audit history.

Data compression.short_definition: Pack/unpack data into compact formats/storage slots to reduce on-chain storage costs.

Data separation.short_definition: Physically separate stored data from manipulating logic to support upgrades and reduce coupling.

Homomorphic encryption.short_definition: Compute over encrypted data without decrypting it.

Zero-knowledge proof.short_definition: Prove a statement without revealing underlying data, with contract verification of the proof.

Commit and Reveal.short_definition: Commit a secret's hash, later reveal the value and verify it matches the prior commitment.

Snapshotting.short_definition: Copy source blockchain states/contracts/transactions for subsequent transfer to a destination chain during migration.

State initialization.short_definition: Transfer and initialize source-chain state on the destination chain during migration.

Establish genesis.short_definition: Initialize a destination blockchain's genesis block with migrated state.

Smart contract translation.short_definition: Adapt existing smart-contract code to a destination blockchain's VM/language during migration.

Tokenization.short_definition: Represent an asset/right/entity as transferable on-chain tokens; listing an existing token alone is insufficient.

Self-generated transactions.short_definition: The user constructs and signs transactions client-side and retains full control of private keys.

Self-Confirmed Transactions.short_definition: The application constructs a transaction; the user manually confirms and signs it with a browser wallet.

Delegated Transactions.short_definition: The application controls blockchain operations, keys and wallets on the user's behalf, requiring trust in the service.

Packing variables.short_definition: Place small typed variables adjacently in the same 32-byte storage slot to reduce storage reads/writes.

Packing booleans.short_definition: Pack multiple boolean values as bits in a bitmap to save storage.

Unit vs Unit256.short_definition: Choose smaller integer types versus uint256 considering packing, storage access and gas costs.

Mapping vs Array.short_definition: Choose Solidity mapping versus array according to data access patterns and gas/storage tradeoffs.

Freeing storage.short_definition: Delete unused storage variables to release storage and obtain applicable gas refunds.
